case_name: State of Uttar Pradesh v Atar Singh and Others
facts: The incident took place on 4.5.1979 at about 6:30 P.M. in village Balli Nagla, Police Station Qadarchowk, District Budaun.
About 6 months before this incident, Durgapal-brother-in-law of Shyam Pal (PW-1) had abducted Dhika daughter of Dallu.
The accused-respondents began to bear ill will against him and his family members on this account.
On 4-5-79 at about 6:30 P.M., exchange of hot words and abuses took place between Shyam Pal (PW-1) and Dallu at the Chaupal of Nek Ram in connection with abduction of Dhika.
Some persons intervened in the matter and Shyam Pal went to his home. A little later, all the accused-respondents along with Dallu entered the house of Shyam Pal.
issues: Motive assigned by the prosecution against the accused respondents
Immediate motive for the alleged occurrence
Corroboration to the prosecution version by any independent witnesses
petitioner_arguments: The prosecution has not been able to substantiate its version.
There was no reason as to why the injured person would falsely implicate the innocent person.
court_reasoning: The High Court noted that the motive assigned by the prosecution against the accused respondents did not stand the test of logic.

The High Court found it hard to believe that after alleged exchange of hot words at the Chaupal of Nek Ram, he with all his sons, brother and nephew would have appeared in the house of PW-1 to assault him and his family members.
The High Court noted that there was no corroboration to the prosecution version by any independent witnesses.
holding: The High Court acquitted the respondents and set aside the conviction recorded by the learned Additional Sessions Judge.
The Supreme Court upheld the acquittal of the respondents.
